tension_sets.claim_A: Successive replacement by synthetic generations can cause collapse and loss of tails.
tension_sets.claim_B: Accumulating original/real data with synthetic data can keep training stable.
tension_sets.resolution: Generational outcome depends on lineage memory: replacement, accumulation, mixing ratio and external grounding must be treated as causal variables.

tension_sets.claim_A: Serial transmission can converge toward stable attractors.
tension_sets.claim_B: Recursive training can accumulate errors and drift away from the ancestor distribution.
tension_sets.resolution: Attraction and drift are not opposites: different observables can converge while other dimensions lose diversity or accumulate error.

tension_sets.claim_A: Individual agents may appear unbiased under isolated evaluation.
tension_sets.claim_B: Populations can develop collective bias during decentralized convention formation.
tension_sets.resolution: Machine psychology requires population-level assays; single-agent measurements are insufficient for emergent social phenotypes.

tension_sets.claim_A: Information can evolve across frozen inference-only chains.
tension_sets.claim_B: Traits can transfer through parameter updates/distillation.
tension_sets.resolution: IO must keep cultural transmission through messages separate from heritable parameter-level transmission; a strong machine-tradition claim requires evidence across both agent replacement and lineage transmission.
